findings.claim: The set's meaning is inverted (allowlist → denylist); every use site must have its predicate flipped or the VM/environment logic silently reverses.
findings.rationale: Before, `DOM_ENVIRONMENTS.has(env)` was true only for jsdom/happy-dom (the environments with a VM upside). Now the set lists the environments *without* upside, so any call site that still reads `SET.has(env)` as "measure VM candidates" will now do exactly the opposite (measuring VM for node/edge-runtime and skipping it for jsdom/happy-dom). The hunk doesn't show the call sites, so I can't confirm they were updated to `!ENVIRONMENTS_WITHOUT_VM_UPSIDE.has(env)` — worth verifying; high impact if missed.

findings.claim: An unset/empty `environment` (which defaults to 'node') is not a member of the new set, so the default project will now be treated as having a VM upside.
findings.rationale: With the old allowlist, `undefined`/`''` fell outside jsdom/happy-dom and VM candidates were correctly skipped. With the denylist, `ENVIRONMENTS_WITHOUT_VM_UPSIDE.has(undefined)` is false, so the most common configuration (no `environment` specified → node) is now classified as VM-worthy. Unless the caller normalizes the value to 'node' before the lookup, this is a real behavior regression. Fairly confident this is a live edge case; depends on unseen normalization.

findings.claim: Treating all unknown/custom environments as VM candidates makes the doctor run fail for custom environments that don't implement `setupVM`, instead of skipping them.
findings.rationale: The added comment explicitly acknowledges "the run fails if they lack setupVM". A diagnostic/advisory command failing hard because a user's custom environment doesn't support VM mode is a poor failure mode; the candidate should either be probed (check for a `setupVM` export) or the measurement failure should be caught and reported as "not applicable" rather than aborting.

findings.claim: Exact-string matching may miss equivalent environment specifiers such as a package-qualified name or path-based custom environment resolving to node.
findings.rationale: Environments can be referenced by package name (e.g. `vitest-environment-node`) or configured per-file via `environmentMatchGlobs`/docblocks; a plain `Set.has()` on the root `environment` string won't catch those and will mis-classify them as VM-worthy. Low confidence that this matters in practice, but the denylist form makes mismatches fail open rather than closed.
